LESSON: READING 9.2.1 EXTENSIVE READING: GRADE APPROPRIATE FICTION MATERIALS - CHARACTERS

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 9
Topic 9.2: Reading 9.2.1 Extensive Reading: Grade appropriate fiction Materials - Characters
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 9.2.1 Extensive Reading: Grade appropriate fiction Materials - Characters, part of Strand 9 in Grade 8 ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: why. 1. What makes reading enjoyable? 2. How can the characters in a story be described? 3. Which stories are the most enjoyable to read?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. search online and offline for words that can be used to describe character traits,
2. read a given fiction material on African heroes/heroines and list the characters in the text,
3. role play the different characters identified,
4. dramatise the text and video record the performance,
5. choose a character and discuss

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 9.2.1 Extensive Reading: Grade appropriate fiction Materials - Characters together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Creativity and imagination: It is developed and networking is enhanced as the learner role plays different characters.

• Digital literacy: It is developed as the learner searches online and video record their performances using their digital devices.

Values:
Social justice: Reading on African heroes/ heroines makes the learner understand issues that Africa as a continent is exposed to

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Citizenship education ( ethnic and racial relations): Reading on African Heroes/ Heroines makes the learner appreciate Africa’s

ethnic diversity.
